input.message:
Dear Mrs Ferris,

Thank you for your patience. Here is what our records show and what a recall would and wouldn't do.

Our account records show a Faster Payment of £651.00 from your account on 12 August 2026 to CO-CLEAN SERVICES LTD, reference "INV 4471 53 WINCHESTER". It went to a new payee, and the Confirmation of Payee check matched at the time. I have asked for the payment journal to be checked as well, but I don't have a result from that check yet. That means I can't yet confirm from our records whether any refund from Co-Clean has reached your account.

Why a recall isn't the right route here: once a Faster Payment has been sent, we can't take it back. A recall is mainly for payments sent to the wrong account or sent in error. All it does is ask the receiving bank to return the money, and that only happens if the account holder agrees. Your payment went to the payee you meant to pay, and the second payment was made separately by your letting agent. Co-Clean has told you they will refund £651, so a recall request would still depend on their agreement. It is unlikely to get your money back faster than the refund they have already promised, and we can't promise that it would.

What this does not mean: we have not made any finding about the payment. We haven't asked for a recall or started a dispute, and we haven't checked Co-Clean's records or your agent's. The email and statement extract you sent us show what Co-Clean and Oakfield PM have said. They are not our records.

What you can do: the quickest route is usually to contact Co-Clean directly about when their next payment run is. Please don't send any further payment for invoice 4471. If the refund doesn't arrive, you can contact us again through the app and we can look at the options with you then.

Kind regards,
Harrow & Vale Bank plc
